messages:
alex_support: Hey team — customer (acct: acme-inc) reports a sudden spike of 502s + intermittent 401s after a model rollout earlier today. Customer supplied two request ids: r-0a1b2c3d and r-7f8e9d0c. They also saw a billing token surge. Need repro steps + debug bundle collection. Can we get a curl they can run and verify whether pinning the stable model removes the failures?

maria_oncall: Thanks — I saw the traces. Canary got ~40% traffic at 09:12 UTC, error rate jumped then. 502s are gateway errors from the serving runtime; 401s are from auth backend failing to validate a subset of tokens (looks intermittent). I suspect a routing mismatch where some requests hit an older auth cache node.

tim_engineering: @maria_oncall can you paste the minimal curl we should have the customer run? Also request the debug bundle and the full X-Request-ID header value for those reqids.

maria_oncall: Minimal curl (send with their actual API key and one of the failing reqids in X-Request-ID):
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xxl-canary","input":"hi"}' \
  --compressed
```
Add `-H "X-Debug: 1"` to trigger expanded logs on our side. Ask them to attach the full client stdout/stderr.

jen_product: Also confirm whether they are using a pinned model in their integration. If they can repro with the canary model name and then again with the stable variant we can confirm the regression surface. Suggested pair of requests to run: `redwood-xxl-canary` and `redwood-xxl-stable:2026-02-14`.

alex_support: I've asked customer for the debug bundle. Requested: curl output, the two request ids, their API key masked, and a timeline of the calls. I already told them to run the curl above.

tim_engineering: If they provide a debug bundle, we want these artifacts: router logs around the reqid, auth service logs for the reqid, and the runtime container stderr/stdout. We can collect from our side with: `sre-bot collect debug --req r-0a1b2c3d` (internal). Please wait for their permission to fetch tenant logs.

maria_oncall: Quick triage notes:
- 502s correlate with a spike of calls that triggered a fallback from the quantized canary (q8) to the stable CPU fallback for a small subset — latency/timeouts then cascaded into gateway 502s.
- 401s appear in a narrow window (09:11:20–09:13:05 UTC) and align with an auth cache TTL refresh that failed for a small fraction of tokens.
- Billing token surge likely from retries — client SDK will retry on 502 and re-send tokens, inflating usage.

tim_engineering: Next steps for repro and mitigation:
1) Customer runs the curl above with `X-Debug: 1` and captures full verbose output.
2) Customer runs two quick calls: canary model and stable pinned model. Example: `-d '{"model":"redwood-xxl-canary","input":"test"}'` then `-d '{"model":"redwood-xxl-stable:2026-02-14","input":"test"}'`.
3) Have them set a static `X-Request-ID` per run so we can match logs.
4) If they prefer immediate mitigation, instruct them to pin to the stable version or temporarily route all traffic off canary (they can change model name in code).

alex_support: Customer asked whether pinning is safe now or if we recommend rollback. They want clarity on whether this was a canary bug or infra auth flakiness.

jen_product: Given current evidence, recommend pin to stable while we finish log analysis. We'll also open a rollback of canary for a short window if we see sustained errors in other tenants.

maria_oncall: I'll start collecting infra traces for the two reqids once customer sends the debug bundle. If we confirm a kernel/quantization regression in canary, we'll tag it as a model-serving regression and block further canary traffic.

sre-bot: NOTE: Please include the following when sending debug bundle to us: environment (host/region), exact API key prefix (masked ok), IPs, and the `X-Request-ID`. Run this on customer side: `tar czf debugbundle-<reqid>.tgz /path/to/client-logs && curl -F file=@debugbundle-<reqid>.tgz https://support-upload.redwood.example/upload`

tim_engineering: If customer can't share a bundle, at least insist on the `curl -v` stdout and the full `X-Request-ID` header values. Those let us pull router traces.

alex_support: I'll update the customer with these steps and ask them to run both curls and upload the bundle. Will paste their reply here. :thumbsup:

jen_product: Thanks — once we have the bundle we'll pivot (pin, rollback, or fix) and update SLA notes if needed.

maria_oncall: One more internal note: watch for auth cache refresh jobs around 09:10–09:14 in EU region; I already created a short alert to monitor error spikes linked to auth cache misses.

alex_support: Customer replied — they ran the canary curl with X-Debug and got `HTTP/2 502` and the full verbose output attached. Also got `401` on a separate token for req `r-7f8e9d0c`. They'll upload the debugbundle now.

maria_oncall: Great — once uploaded I will run `sre-bot collect debug --req r-0a1b2c3d r-7f8e9d0c` and share the traces here.

tim_engineering: If we confirm canary-induced fallback, actionable fixes: revert kernel change in canary, tighten fallback thresholds (avoid CPU fallback for short tails), and patch auth cache refresh race.

alex_support: Filing a follow-up ticket with the customer outcome after we analyze. Leaving this thread open until traces and decision.

sre-bot: Incident stub created: INC-2026-0427-001. Assigned to maria_oncall + tim_engineering.
